items.summary: OpenHands published as conference paper at ICLR 2025.
OpenHands preprint posted to arXiv with identifier 2407.16741v3.
OpenHands has received 32K GitHub stars and 2.1K contributions from 188+ contributors.
items.notes: Authors state 'more than 2.1K contributions from over 188 contributors' and '32K GitHub stars' in abstract and introduction

items.notes: Section 4.2.1 notes this is significantly better than non-agentic approaches and almost doubles StarCoder2-15B performance

items.summary: OpenHands supports 15 benchmarks across software engineering, web browsing, and miscellaneous assistance.
Authors hypothesize OpenHands enables systematic evaluation to identify and address agent risks before deployment.
items.notes: Section B Ethics Statement states OpenHands helps mitigate risks by enabling systematic evaluation

items.summary: Current agents still struggle with complex tasks and file editing on long files.
items.notes: Authors identify agent file editing and multi-modality as areas needing improvement

items.summary: OpenHands workflow currently requires substantial handcrafted workload.
items.notes: Authors propose graph-based frameworks as alternative for automatic workflow generation

items.summary: CodeActAgent v1.8 with gpt-4o-mini achieves only 6.3% on SWE-Bench Lite (compared to 26.0% with claude-3.5-sonnet).
SWE-Bench Lite evaluation cost estimate: approximately $6.9k for all 2294 instances.
items.notes: Authors provide cost context for evaluation decisions

items.summary: HumanEvalFix evaluation uses 0-shot approach with agent self-debugging over multiple turns.
items.notes: Section 4.2.1 explicitly states OpenHands evaluation is 0-shot vs SWE-Agent's 1-shot

items.summary: BIRD evaluation removes original prompts to demonstrate OpenHands context retrieval capability.
items.notes: Demonstrates experimental modification to evaluate specific capabilities

items.summary: OpenHands runtime uses dual-tagging system for Docker images: hash-based and generic tags.
items.notes: Section F.2.1 describes hash-based (reproducibility) and generic (latest version) tags

items.summary: Integration test framework uses LLM mocking with exact prompt matches for deterministic behavior.
items.notes: Section E describes integration testing with foundation model mocking

items.summary: Authors assume downstream agents will trust and rely on OpenHands outputs.
items.notes: Implicit in framework design emphasizing reliable output formats

items.summary: CodeActAgent designed as generalist agent across software, web, and misc tasks.
items.notes: Table 3 showcases competitive performance on 3 major task categories without modification

items.summary: HumanEvalFix benchmark allows achieving 100% with bug-free implementations.
items.notes: Authors note 79.3% is achievable for 100% in future iterations

items.summary: OpenHands released under permissive MIT license.
